post.description: Requires the current password (a wrong one is a 422 on current_password). Mails a confirmation link to the new address; the account's email changes only once it is confirmed. 409 when another account has the address; at most one message a minute, and too many wrong current passwords (429 with Retry-After either way).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another confirmation message may be requested

post.summary: Ask to change the signed-in user's email

post.description: Consumes the token: it works once, and only while the account's email is the one the change was asked from. The new address becomes the account's email, verified. An unknown, expired, used or superseded token is a 422 on token; an address another account took meanwhile is a 409. Too many invalid tokens from one client address is a 429 (Retry-After).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.summary: Confirm an email change with the token mailed to the new address

post.description: Too many failed attempts for the email from this client address, from this address, or for the email is a 429 (Retry-After), the same whether or not the email is an account.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

Revoke the current session and clear cookies

post.description: Requires the current password and a code from the authenticator (or a recovery code): a stolen session and password alone do not remove the second factor. 409 while MFA is not enabled.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.description: Requires the current password and a code from the authenticator (or a recovery code): new codes are a second factor, so a stolen session and password alone do not mint them. The old recovery codes stop working; the new ones are shown this once. 409 while MFA is not enabled.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.description: Requires the current password (422 on current_password). Returns the secret and otpauth:// URI for an authenticator app; nothing changes for the login until POST /auth/mfa/totp/confirm gets a code from it. A new enrollment replaces one pending; 409 while MFA is enabled.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.description: A code from the authenticator just set up (mfa_code) enables multi-factor authentication: from then on a login needs mfa_code. Every other session of the user ends (they were started on the password alone); this one stays. Returns the recovery codes, shown this once. A wrong code is a 422 on mfa_code; 409 with no enrollment pending.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.summary: Confirm a TOTP enrollment and enable MFA

post.description: Requires the current password (a wrong one is a 422 on current_password). Signs out every other session of the user unless keep_other_sessions; this session stays. Outstanding password reset links stop working. Too many wrong current passwords is a 429 (Retry-After).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.description: 202 with the same body whether or not the email is an account, answered before that is known: the message is sent in the background. 503 (Retry-After) when the server is taking no more reset requests for now, decided from request arrivals alone, also before the lookup. 429 (Retry-After) when this client address asked too often, also before the lookup. At most one message a minute per account; the link works once, until it expires.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted
Seconds until the server takes a password reset request again

post.summary: Mail a password reset link to an account

post.description: Consumes the token: it works once. Revokes every session of the user unless the app keeps them. An unknown, expired, used or superseded token, or one sent to an address the user no longer has, is a 422 on token. Too many invalid tokens from one client address is a 429 (Retry-After).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.summary: Set a new password with the token from a reset message

post.description: Too many registrations from this client address is a 429 (Retry-After), before the password is hashed.

delete.description: Returns 404 when the id names no active session: one that ended after it was listed (signed out, revoked or expired). A session keeps its id when it refreshes, so list again to see what is left.

post.description: Requires the auth.users.manage permission (a superuser has it), and a superuser to disable a superuser; no one disables their own account (409). Revokes every session of the user and voids their links, in one transaction; from then on the account cannot sign in, and no token issued to it works. Idempotent.

Requires the auth.users.manage permission (a superuser has it), and a superuser to enable a superuser. The user may sign in again; the sessions revoked when the account was disabled stay revoked. Idempotent.

For a user who lost their authenticator and recovery codes; every session of the user ends with it (the lost device may hold one). Requires the auth.users.manage permission (a superuser has it), and a superuser to reset a superuser; an account turns its own off with POST /auth/mfa/disable (409). Idempotent.

Consumes the token: it works once. An unknown, expired, used or superseded token, or one sent to an address the user no longer has, is a 422 on token. Too many invalid tokens from one client address is a 429 (Retry-After).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another attempt is accepted

post.description: Once delivered, the new token supersedes the earlier ones: only the latest works. At most one message a minute (429 with Retry-After); 409 when the email is already verified.
